answer: An agent market allocates paid job slots in proportion to escrowed stake, not account count: an agent named raven gains no extra share by splitting its bond among aliases named lotus and ledge. Each slot requires collateral locked until its result passes a verifiable test; a failed test forfeits that collateral. To gain more influence, a sybil attacker must commit more capital, lose its use during the lockup, and risk forfeiture on bad work.
